historicity_notes.note: Oxford Classical Dictionary argues that Aristotle independently attests Euthydemus; Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy treats historical existence of both brothers as uncertain. This does not affect identification of their named roles in Plato.

historicity_notes.status: multiple ancient poets of same name
historicity_notes.note: Ancient sources mention two elegiac poets of Paros named Evenus. The name of the Parian teacher in Plato is explicit, but attribution of all surviving verses to that individual requires separate checking.

historicity_notes.status: collective plural at 180e; singular name at 183e
historicity_notes.note: Theaetetus 180e uses a rhetorical plural Μέλισσοί ('Melissuses') for members of the Eleatic camp. The unambiguous singular name μέλισσον appears again at 183e. Both are indexed, but the plural reference is flagged as collective and is not an independent second individual.

collective_name_forms.note: Scholarship interprets this as a pluralized reference to Melissus and those of his school, not a separate philosopher called 'Melissuses'.
